While you wait

Four things we do at the counter.

Not everything here is a rental. Some of it you bring in and take back out fixed.

Hydraulic hoses

We build them here. Bring in the blown hose and the fittings go on while you're standing there.

Chainsaw chains

Sharpened, or built new to your bar length.

Mower blades

Drop them off dull. Pick them up sharp, before the grass gets ahead of you.

Propane & kerosene

Bulk fills, seven days a week — the reason half of Buckley knows where we are in January.

Before you drive out

How renting here works.

  • ✓Reservations are free, by phone. We gladly take phoned-in reservations. We don't take online reservations — a person picks up.
  • ✓Be 18, bring your driver's license. That's the ID we rent against.
  • ✓A deposit based on your rental time. All major credit cards accepted.
  • ✓No extra fuel surcharges. Deliveries quoted when you need the machine brought to you.
  • ✓Not sure what you need? Just ask. The crew will recommend the right tool for the project — and the coffee's always on.

Since August 2002

You may know it as the Old Shake Mill.

Victor Proulx and Gail Bohnas — long-time Bonney Lake residents — opened the doors on August 31, 2002.

The building sawed cedar shakes and boards through the 1970s, and there's still a wall of shakes and boards standing in the office. The counter you lean on was built for Nordstrom in the late seventies by Custom Craft Fixtures, bought by a Farmers Insurance agency in Bonney Lake around 1983, and picked up by us when that agency moved to Sumner.

The rest of the walls are neighbours. The horse collar and hames came from Sue Carson, off an old farm outside Kalispell, Montana on the Farm to Market Road. The bridle came from Larry Carson, out of Spanaway. The hay hooks and wooden pulleys are from the family farm in Winlock. We change the decorations around now and then.
